# Incident with Pull Requests, Git Operations and Issues

## What Changed

Nov 4, 11:50 UTC Resolved - n November 4, 2026, between 09:35 UTC and 11:43 UTC, customers experienced intermittent errors and timeouts across GitHub.com, primarily on actions that write data. At peak, about 20% of pull request write operations (such as merging, commenting, and reviewing) failed, along with about 10% of issue creates and edits and 10–15% of project item edits. Git pushes over SSH, REST and GraphQL API requests, code scanning uploads, releases, and package operations were also affected, and about 1% of Actions runs were delayed by more than five minutes or failed to start. Overall, nearly 4% of all requests to GitHub.com failed at the worst point. Reads were largely unaffected, and retrying a failed action a short time later usually succeeded. The incident was triggered by a burst of concurrent updates to the same database record, which tied up all available connections to one of our primary databases. Although that contention cleared, the backlog of waiting requests kept our database connection layer overloaded, and it did not recover on its own.
